shortDescription: Woodward NASDAQ:WWD said Monday it plans to shut a production facility in Santa Clarita, California, and move production of military fixed-wing and rotorcraft flight control actuation to its campus in Spartanburg, South Carolina, as part of its efforts to streamline its portfolio and refine its man…

children: a production facility in Santa Clarita, California, and move production of military fixed-wing and rotorcraft flight control actuation to its campus in Spartanburg, South Carolina, as part of its efforts to streamline its portfolio and refine its manufacturing footprint.

said it agreed to sell a smaller group of legacy commercial rotorcraft, land systems, and business jet products made in Santa Clarita, along with the campus itself, in a transaction expected to close no later than year-end 2027, affecting ~400 positions.
The company said it expects to recognize pre-tax charges of $34M-$47.5M in connection with the closing, due mostly to employee-related costs and contract terminations.

The Spartanburg plant is expected to begin operations in summer 2027, producing Airbus A350 spoiler actuation systems in addition to the transferred product lines and other aerospace components, the company said.

title: Woodward to close California plant, shift production to South Carolina
